precepts.text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee. The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. You know which sins you deal with, yet you still entertain them.
precepts.point: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out. We got to repent as a nation, and in the context of this topic, repent from alcoholism. It is not something you can play with; you cannot play with sin.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
“Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out”. We have to repent as a nation, and in the context of this class, repent from alcoholism. You have to stop. It is not something you can play with. You cannot play with sin.

That is why God says, “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee”. It will bite you. You do not stand close to a serpent and see how long you can last; you flee from it.

“The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” That is sin. It is going into the sins you know you deal with. You know which particular sins you struggle with, and yet you still entertain them.

Deacon Joshua said it: you should be able to go six months. Just drop it for six months. Especially you big brothers: drop the alcohol for six months and watch how fast you get in the green, because every week you take away 4,000 calories. To repent and be converted is to flee from the bottle, not to keep it near and hope it does not bite.

precepts.text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: that's what Joseph did. If thou comest too near it, it will bite thee. The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. If a snake fell in this room right now, everybody would be out of here. That snake is your sin.
precepts.point: Everybody's demon is not the same. For some it's food, but generally it's sexual demons that get the brothers. Take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did.
precepts.why:
Potiphar’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Lie with me.” Joseph refused, and he did not refuse half-heartedly: “how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Notice he was not blaming God that he was a slave in a strange land. His master had kept nothing back from him “but thee, because thou art his wife,” and Joseph would not touch her.

This was not a single moment. “she spake to Joseph day by day”; she was trying to wear him down day by day. And the Egyptians loved beautiful women; remember when Abraham went down into Egypt, Sarah was in danger because of her beauty. Potiphar’s wife was no ugly woman; she was good on the eyes, and Joseph, at 17 years old, still said no. When she finally “caught him by his garment,” “he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.”

Sirach gives the precept for what Joseph did: “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” Joseph saw sin like a snake, and he ran like a rabbit. If a snake fell into the room right now, everybody would be out of there. That snake is your sin. “All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.”

Everybody's demon is not the same. For some it is food; for most of the brothers it is sexual demons, and those demons will get you. Put yourself in Joseph's place and be honest about it: many have been put out for adultery two and three times. Take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did: don't stand there and reason with it, don't come near it. Flee.

precepts.text: When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul: you will have brothers and sisters say the wicked are going to be destroyed, and meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. You curse Satan and curse your own soul, because when you become overcome with it you take on the same attributes Cain did. We have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offense, and deal with our brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God; do not let it fester and resonate in your spirit.
precepts.point: He that loveth not his brother abideth in death: that brother's home is death. Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
John says “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Even the scribes and Pharisees took on the spirit of Cain, of Satan; they moved in the same exact spirit, bitter toward Christ and wanting to put him to death. That spirit will jump on us too, and we have to deal with it. When we are overcome with it, we take on the same attributes Cain did.

“When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” You will have brothers and sisters say, the white man is the devil, they're going to be destroyed, they're going into captivity. And meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. So you curse Satan, and you curse your own soul, because you have hatred toward your brother. Brothers talk bold against the white man and find themselves in the same spirit as him.

“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” Whoever is bitter toward his brother is in the spirit of Cain; you are in the same spirit. That hatred is always masked: “Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” He acted like his friend to get him in position.

So we have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offence. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God. Don't allow it to fester and resonate in your spirit until you are overcome, because “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.”

precepts.text: The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel; he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth. A skilful man hears a wise word and commends it; one of no understanding hears it, it displeaseth him, and he casts it behind his back. That is why the foolishness pours out of their mouths.
precepts.point: Nobody questions these men because the souls following them are unstable and cannot go to the book and study to show themselves approved. An heart exercised with covetous practices, cursed children, which have forsaken the right way. The right way is to keep the commandments without adding an alternate reality to fit what you want.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
This is sad. These brothers have lost all wisdom out of their vessel, if they ever obtained it. Look at what we are doing: the secret sauce is keeping the commandments. Just follow the blueprint.

“The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.” That is why you see foolishness spewing out of their mouths: as was supposed, a whole podcast of it, jargon and foolishness with nothing held inside.

“If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add unto it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.” If a man of no understanding hears the commandments and that he must keep them, it displeases him, and he casts them behind his back. That is what we are looking at right now. He has cast off the law and forsaken the right way, like Peter says, and so all manner of foolishness comes out of these brothers' mouths. That line will not go throughout the earth at all.

precepts.text: He that is not wise will not be taught, but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness: seeing it your own way. Sirach 3:26, a stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.
precepts.point: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened. Leaven grows.
precepts.why:
Some don't want to be taught, and Sirach says why: “He that is not wise will not be taught”. If you're a fool, it doesn't matter what somebody does for you; you will not be taught, you will not retain it, it's not going to work for you.

“but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness”. That wisdom is seeing it your own way, doing your own thing, and you're going to have a bitter end because of it.

Sirach 3:26 shows that bitterness: “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”. You're stubborn and don't want to learn; when wise words come out you're in the back, or you've got that hatred, something against somebody, so you don't want to hear nothing from them. And “he that loveth danger shall perish therein”. People like that are very dangerous; they can get people hurt if you follow after them. They perish in their folly, because they are unwise and not taught, because fools despise knowledge.

precepts.text: My son, prove thy soul and thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it; for all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing. Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. It is literally about food, and spiritually about proving your spirit: see what is evil for you and give it not, whether a food or a show like Spartacus full of sex scenes. A fat brother's diet is different from a slim officer's.
precepts.point: The Lord is using Captain Shem's initiative with the yellow and red brothers for your health, because we need brothers fit and in the street to teach. Knowing it is not good for you and still indulging shows you lack discipline; a man who cannot control his own thoughts accomplishes nothing.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee.” We usually use flee for lust, but you cannot flee from something that is in your refrigerator or your freezer. The brain does not distinguish: the same dopamine and reward centers fire for food that pleases the flesh as for sex. Flee from the unhealthy foods, or they bite you and destroy you. That is why so many brothers have health issues, in the hospital every week and unable to make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Sirach goes further: “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.” From verse 27 down to 30 it is literally about food, and spiritually it is about proving your spirit. Just as you see which foods make you sick and unhealthy, see what things are evil for you and make you mentally unhealthy, and give not that unto it. Spartacus was a good show, with a whole lot of sex scenes; you may have to say, I can’t watch this.

“For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” A fat brother’s diet is different from a slim officer’s. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” Don’t overindulge beyond your limits, and don’t eat excessively.

Food porn works on the brain the same way pornography does, because the brain sees both as nourishment. There is a healthy pleasure and an unhealthy one: healthy food instead of junk, your wife instead of the screen. Peter says, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. When you are counting calories and a 240-calorie cookie calls you with 100 left, you feel that war inside. It is the same temptation, a worldly lust we inherited through America.

“By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Lord is putting us on another level of discipline, because we need brothers fit and in the street teaching.

precepts.text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; come too near and it will bite thee. Joseph fled.
precepts.point: That is the example: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee; the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion. Joseph knew thirty more seconds of entertaining her would be the bite.
precepts.why:
“My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins. Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.”

That is exactly what Joseph did. She spake to him day by day and he hearkened not; then she arranged the empty house, caught him by his garment and said “Lie with me”, and “he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.” He did not stand and reason with her. He fled from sin as from the face of a serpent.

Joseph knew that thirty more seconds of entertaining her would be the bite. Come too near sin and it will bite thee, and its teeth are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. That is the example: flee.

precepts.text: My son, have you sinned? Do so no more, and pray pardon for your former sins; flee from sin as from a serpent.
precepts.point: Many of us are still plagued by things from our past even in the truth, whether health issues like cancer or an STD, or the burden of having children with a wicked woman and enduring her wickedness. You bear that cross and follow Christ.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David prays, “judge me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me.” Ecclesiasticus tells you how to get there: “My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins. Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.”

This is your prayer: ask the Lord to judge you based on your righteousness and the integrity now in you, and to pardon your former sins. Have you sinned? Do so no more, and flee from sin as from a serpent, because if you come too near it, it will bite you.

Many of us are still plagued by things from our past even in the truth, whether health issues like cancer or an STD, or the burden of having children with a wicked woman and enduring her wickedness. The serpent bit, and the teeth are as the teeth of a lion. You bear that cross and follow Christ, asking pardon for the former sins and doing so no more.

points: All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed. We just read that the word of God is a twoedged sword that cures, so why can these wounds not be healed? Verse six answers: he that hateth to be reproved is in the way of sinners, but he that feareth the Lord will repent from his heart. The wounds cannot be healed because you hate to be reproved. The word of God cuts, but you can be healed if you accept what it is saying. That means somebody is telling you, and you are listening.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent. You have to get away from that thing. You do not negotiate with temptation; you flee immediately. If it seems wrong, get away from it. If you have any doubt about the judgment you are about to commit, leave it alone; that means something is not right with it.

Satan does not force sin. He might suggest it, wrap it up in something else, beautify it, rationalize it; but ultimately you have to agree with it. So do not let Satan give you that kiss on the cheek. It is not always good.

Doctrine unto fools is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand. The laws of God, to a fool, feel like being handcuffed and imprisoned. I agree with the history but not the theology: because the commandments of God are fetters and manacles to them. Keeping God's laws is prison to their mind, so they stay to themselves.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: He that keepeth the law of the Lord getteth the understanding thereof: that is how you start to understand what God is really saying and how it pertains to you. And the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.

In studying the law, in getting around your brothers and sisters, in seeking counsel, you start to perfect your fear of the Lord. Because contrary to popular belief, your sin does not just happen: you entertain it, you put it there, you leave it there, you make provision for it, because there is no fear.

Everybody that came into this truth could not put the Bible down at first: video after video, highlighters, up all night. Then it starts to get regular, and you start to not read as much, not study as much, not even pray. We have seen brothers and sisters that were doing well; then life came, sin started to happen, they got wrapped up in it, and they are unrecognizable now. That is why we say like David: Lord, please do not take your Holy Spirit from me.

We all are going to struggle with something, but the point is to struggle with it; do not let it defeat you. All manner of sin shall be forgiven; a brother dealing with drunkenness does not need to exile himself from the body. Israel United in Christ is built off the betterment of the souls of God's people, for you to grow and get better from your sin.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

Flee the unhealthy foods, or they bite: brothers with health problems in the hospital every week who cannot make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Eating one meal a day did not work until the type of food changed, because preservatives and chemicals cannot break down. There is no such thing as the itis; the food makes you sleepy, and after a big meal in Japan we felt more awake and alert, which is what food is supposed to do. Categorizing calories, protein, fats, and fiber within a window became cross-discipline that carried into study habits, lust, and dealing with people.

The Lord is using Captain Shem's initiative with the yellow and red brothers for your health, because we need brothers fit and in the street to teach. Knowing it is not good for you and still indulging shows you lack discipline; a man who cannot control his own thoughts accomplishes nothing.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

points: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee. Do not caress or charm it. A coiled snake's striking distance is longer than you think, and by the time you take two steps back it has you. Joseph did not stand there; he ran.

The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. The devil is the roaring lion of 1 Peter 5:8, smelling everyone daily until one day something is different about you, and then you are done.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood. You see that? The knowledge of a wise man. You are steadily meditating, you are reading, it is going to abound with you like a flood overflowing. That water just overflowing in the mind. Christ said it is like springs from the belly.

And his counsel is like a pure fountain of life. His counsel is like that pure fountain of life right there. Like you find a well. You brothers as farmers, you go out there looking for land, you find an open well and they have got a water source. That is the equivalent of finding a good counsellor. Somebody you know that is keeping the commandments, that is going to steer you in the right direction. That is that knowledge of the Lord. That is the stability of the times.
The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel. A broken container that cannot hold that wax. The stem is not beneficial because the wax is coming out of that thing. Wax all over the place.

And he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth. No matter how much water you pour into this broken vessel, how much wax you pour into this broken vessel, the container is corrupted. So the Lord is saying your spirit is like the candle of the Lord. You have got to ignite it, and you have got to have these three components, and they all work in tandem together. They all have got to be strong together.
